data.name: Alastair
data.gender_notes: Alastair is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Scottish Gaelic name 'Álasdair', meaning 'Ruler, Defender'. This name was traditionally given to Scottish boys, and was popularized in the English-speaking world through the works of Sir Walter Scott. The name Alastair carries the meaning “Ruler, Defender” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alastair usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, defender and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Alastair belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler, Defender.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alastair total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Alastair is a classical and formal name with a rich heritage rooted in the Scottish Gaelic culture. Its association to the Celtic patron saint Saint Alban and the traditional idea of the name as a defender, makes it a name that evokes a sense of strength and heroism. In modern times, its usage has been adopted beyond the Scottish culture and has become a name for individuals seeking a unique and classy moniker.
data.spiritual_significance: Alastair holds deep spiritual significance as it is believed to be a name bestowed with the power of protection and leadership. Its origins in the Celtic tradition, which was renowned for its connection to the spiritual world, adds an air of mysticism and closeness to the natural elements. For those who bear the name, it carries the reminder of a divine calling to be a defender, a protector, or a leader in their personal lives and in their communities.
